newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia reforms air route rights system.
newsitem.headline: Australia reforms air route rights system.

text.p: Australia on Wednesday announced reforms to its system for awarding international air route rights, including priority for carriers operating their own services rather than code-sharing.
Transport Minister John Sharp said international air freight rights would be brought under the control of the International Air Services Commission, which already oversees passenger routes.
Freight services, which have increased tenfold under the year-old conservative government, are currently awarded by the Transport Department.
The move will help new freight carriers benefit from the commission's guidelines which give greater weight to new entrants, Sharp said.
The reforms were aimed at boosting freight operations and fostering competition in the passenger and freight markets, he said.

"Australian carriers proposing to operate scheduled international services in their own right will be given priority over competing applicants who propose to code-share with other airlines," he said in a statement.
Code-sharing is a system where an airline sells seats under its own name, but on another carrier.

The commission was established in 1992 to handle applications by airlines to use Australia's international air rights, negotiated between governments, after Canberra ended Qantas Airways Ltd's international monopoly.

Sharp said the government would also give the commission the power to allocate so-called beyond rights, the right of a carrier from one country to take passengers or freight from a second country to a third.
